title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. It is the verso, printed upside down, of a typescript page reused as scrap paper: page 34 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). The neighbouring handwritten pages, on truncations of graded modules over divided-power polynomial rings, are on the other sides of such sheets.

The text proves the semi-stable reduction theorem for abelian varieties (SGA 7 IX, 3.6) by reducing it to an ℓ-adic monodromy statement (3.7).

1. Setting. S is a connected noetherian normal scheme of dimension 1 with function field K, and A_K is an abelian variety over K. Fix a separable closure K̄ and write it as the union of its finite Galois subextensions K_i. Let S_i be the normalization of S in K_i. Let U be the largest open set of S over which A_K has good reduction.

2. Reduction to a trait (spectrum of a discrete valuation ring). Since U is non-empty, T = S − U is a finite set of closed points, and each local ring O_{S,t} is a discrete valuation ring. For each t in T it suffices to find an index i(t) such that A_{K_{i(t)}} is semi-stable at the points of S_{i(t)} above t. One then takes K' to be the compositum of the K_{i(t)}, using that semi-stable reduction is preserved under further extension.

3. One point suffices, and Galois is not needed. Gal(K_i/K) permutes the points above the closed point s, so semi-stability at one point gives it at all of them. It is enough to find a finite separable extension K' with semi-stable reduction at one point of the normalization S'; its Galois closure then also works.

4. Translation. By criterion 3.5(iv), semi-stable reduction means the inertia group I acts on T_ℓ(A(K̄)) unipotently of echelon 2, i.e. (σ−1)^2 = 0 for all σ in I. Theorem 3.6 therefore becomes Corollary 3.7: on a trait there is an open subgroup I' of I acting unipotently of echelon 2 on T_ℓ.

This is Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy proof of the semi-stable reduction theorem, as published in SGA 7 I.
errors: Typescript typos only: 'comme de groupe Gal(K'/K)' should read 'comme le groupe Gal(K_i/K)' (the extension in question at that point is K_i, not yet K'); 'de point fermés' should read 'de points fermés'. The mathematics is correct and matches the published SGA 7 IX §3.

ideas.what: Reduction of the semi-stable reduction theorem from a Dedekind base to a trait, via normalization in finite Galois subextensions and a compositum over the finitely many bad points
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's semi-stable reduction theorem (reduction to the local case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7, 1967-69); Mumford in characteristic 0 / Deligne-Mumford for curves

ideas.what: Semi-stable reduction is equivalent to the inertia acting unipotently of echelon 2 on T_ℓ; it holds after passing to an open subgroup of inertia
ideas.modern_name: Galois criterion for semi-stable reduction / ℓ-adic monodromy theorem for abelian varieties

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript leaf of the published SGA 7 IX, reused as scrap paper for the 1976 notes. Its content is exactly the published text. The only point of interest is archival: the divided-power de Rham notes were written on the backs of SGA 7 typescript sheets.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down and is typescript (SGA 7 IX, p. 34), not manuscript belonging to the cote's subject.
'comme de groupe Gal(K'/K)' is a typo in the original typescript; the intended reading is 'comme le groupe Gal(K_i/K)'.
Handwritten archive numbers on the page: 352 (written twice, alongside a printed 352 label) and 662.
